description:
More than twenty ignored tests across the coding crate carry no reason string, one records its cost in a code comment instead of an annotation, and six use the wrong capitalisation. Make every ignore annotation self-describing and consistently tagged.

## Background

The project tags ignored tests by why they are skipped: `slow:` for tests that exceed the fast tier, `external:` for tests needing hardware or data the checkout does not carry, and `sim:` for long simulation runs. The tag is what lets a reader tell an expensive test from an unrunnable one.

Bare annotations appear across nine test and source files, concentrated in the DVB-T2 verification suite, the test-vector parser and loader, backend integration, LDPC validation and core, and the 5G NR regression suite. One test in the BCJR module records an approximate runtime in a leading comment rather than in the annotation. Six annotations in the LDPC cache I/O tests use a capitalised prefix where the project standard is lowercase.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Every ignored test in gf2-coding carries a reason string opening with a lowercase `slow:`, `external:`, or `sim:` tag.
- [hard] REQ-02: The tag chosen for each test reflects why it is actually skipped, and the text after the tag names the cost or the missing prerequisite.
- [hard] REQ-03: The BCJR test that records its runtime in a comment carries that information in its reason string instead, and the comment is removed.
- [hard] REQ-04: The six capitalised prefixes in the LDPC cache I/O tests are lowercase.
- [hard] REQ-05: No bare ignore attribute remains anywhere in gf2-coding.
- [hard] REQ-06: The set of tests that run in the fast tier is unchanged, the tier stays inside its time budgets, and clippy with warnings denied plus formatting pass.
title: Give every ignored gf2-coding test a tagged reason string
